newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Dlr/mark vols rise after French left win.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Dlr/mark vols rise after French left win.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar/mark options were bid up Monday after a victory of the left in French legislative elections added to uncertainty about the future of a common currency in Europe.

The left's upset win on Sunday initially bolstered the mark, but the currency subsequently slipped as analysts interpreted the election results as increasing the likelihood of a broad economic and monetary union including Italy and Spain that could weaken the euro.

Still weighing on the mark was fallout from the Bundesbank disagreement with Bonn that erupted last week over the government's plan to revalue gold and currency reserves at higher levels to help Germany cut its debt and meet EMU criteria. Finance Minister Theo Waigel said Monday the plan would proceed even without Bundesbank support.
Spot dollar/mark pushed above 1.73 marks in Europe, boosting volatility across the curve, traders noted.
A big buyer in one-year 35-delta mark and Swiss franc puts was credited with prodding volatilities higher by aggressively pursuing upwards of $500 million worth of the options.
"Without that large buying, volatility probably wouldn't be up as much," said a trader for a German bank in New York.
Furthermore, a lack of upside followthrough that left dollar/mark unable to challenge resistance near 1.7360-70 tempered interest in options, said a Chicago-based broker for a European bank.
Still, one-month 25-delta risk reversals for dollar/mark options were reflecting the shift to a higher dollar bias, tilting 0.2/0.5 in favor of mark puts after hovering around par last week.
At midday, one-month dollar/mark implied volatility was up about 0.4 point from Friday at 10.0/10.3 percent, while one-year was 0.2 point higher at 9.5/9.7 percent.
Dollar/yen volatilities dipped as the spot remained quiet, drawing attention to the narrowing vol spreads between the two currency pairs, analysts said.

"People are starting to wonder if dollar/yen vols will go under dollar/mark vols," the Chicago broker said. However, a spot decline below 115.00 yen could quickly alter the scenario by reigniting dollar/yen volatility, he added.
The dollar was hovering at 116.60 yen at midday.
One-month implied volatility for dollar/yen was down 0.2 point at 10.4/10.7 percent, and one-year was off 0.3 point at 9.8/10.1 percent.
Risk reversals for one-month 25-delta options retained their strong bent for yen calls at 0.9/1.2 percent.
